s: A managed front door that turns raw requests into authenticated, rate-limited, routed calls to your backend services.
w: Every client request terminates at the gateway first. It authenticates the caller (API keys, JWT validation), enforces quotas, applies routing rules (path or header based), can transform payloads, and then forwards to internal services. Because it sits on the hot path it is usually deployed redundantly across zones and kept stateless so any instance can serve any request.
use: You expose a public API consumed by third parties or mobile apps and need one stable contract while backends evolve behind it
Multiple microservices need shared cross-cutting behavior (auth, rate limiting, request logging) without reimplementing it everywhere
You must version APIs (v1/v2) and migrate clients gradually
Different consumer tiers (free/pro/enterprise) get different quotas and SLAs
Internal services should never be internet-exposed; the gateway is the only ingress
avoid: Ultra-low-latency internal service-to-service hops where an extra network hop adds measurable p99
Heavy per-request business logic or data transformation - gateways are policy engines, not application servers
Tiny single-service deployments where nginx alone would be cheaper and simpler

props.auth_provider: Which identity source validates tokens before forwarding

size.rps_per_instance: Requests handled per gateway instance per second (default 50k)
size.default_instances: Gateways are critical-path - default 2 for redundancy

pat.d: One gateway per client type (mobile, web, partner) each exposing exactly the shape that client needs.
Route legacy paths to the old system and new paths to new services from the same gateway while migrating.

pits: Gateway as bottleneck - every request funnels through it; scale horizontally and health-check it like a tier-0 service
Config mistakes take down everything at once - stage route changes, canary them, keep rollback instant
Latency tax - usually 1-5ms added; measure p99 through the gateway not just backend latency
tips: Say explicitly: gateway owns POLICY (auth, limits), services own LOGIC
Mention it decouples client contract from internal topology - reorganizations stay invisible to clients
If asked about cost: managed gateways charge per million requests - at very high scale self-hosted nginx/Kong wins
